_comment: Carry destination for the round-5 governance/record findings (#1301, R5-D11-02
and #1303, R5-D13-01). Round 5 filed 48 findings as #1293-#1340 and no umbrella
issue of its own, so the destination is #201 -- the audit programme's standing
tracking issue, the one that received round 5's own round-end comment -- and no
roster group in this tree claims it. Shape and required fields:
stage: any later seat that stamps a release (tools/release/stamp.py, the deploy-key tag push of docs/decisions/0009 step 5); and the D13 dimension of a later audit round (tools/audit/briefs/D13.md is its method, tools/audit/round5/D13/seat-a/dora_cfr.py its harness)

carries.from: the round-5 D11-02 finding (#1301), whose fix is rule "rows" in tools/release/stamp.py -- the stamp now re-applies `record`'s own predicate to the window it is about to close
carries.control: The window `<last v* tag>..origin/main` is the window `record` reads, and the tag push is main-protect's only bypass, so one stamp can carry every rowless merge behind the new tag out of every future window at once. Established by measurement, not argument: the finding's harness (tools/audit/round5/D11/seat-b/corpus_churn.py) reads the same counts at origin/main before this fix and at this fix's head, and the number that matters is the INSTRUMENT's, not the harness's -- `python3 tests/delivery_status.py --check` exits 0 over a window whose merges are minutes old, because at stamp time every merge is PENDING and `--check` refuses only OVERDUE and UNCHECKED; the new `--require-rows` exits 1 over the same ledger and names the rowless merges. The perturbation that would have voided it: a row added for one window merge moves the count by exactly one. The fix is measurement-neutral by construction -- corpus_churn.py prints byte-identical RESULT lines at the pre-fix and post-fix heads, which is the null control separating `--require-rows` (reading the ledger under a stricter bar) from a change to the ledger itself.
carries.remeasure: At your own merge base: `python3 tests/delivery_status.py --check` and `python3 tests/delivery_status.py --require-rows` over the same tree, then `python3 tools/audit/round5/D11/seat-b/corpus_churn.py`. They agree on every verdict but PENDING, and that single disagreement is the whole finding; a later round that reads them as the same predicate has re-derived the escape.
carries.brief: Stamp-time precondition, not an opportunity: `tools/release/stamp.py` REFUSES to stamp when any merged pull request in the window it would close has no disposition row, and the only override is the explicit `--allow-rowless` flag, which prints the instrument's own output before proceeding. The rows it demands are the ones `record` demands, on the same two surfaces tests/delivery_status.py's DISPOSITION_FILES names. A stamp over a rowless window is no longer an ordinary release step: it is a knowingly deferred batch, and it is recorded as one. The re-application lives in the stamp's module docstring as rule "rows", so a seat that reads the contract rather than the flag sees it before it runs.

carries.from: the round-5 D13-01 finding (#1303), whose fix makes the CFR exclusion list a registered in-tree artifact that the instrument reads from the repository root, failing closed when it is absent
carries.control: The finding: the round-5 harness opened `cfr_exclusions.json` beside itself, so `cfr_excluded` came from a file the tree did not carry -- and tools/audit/briefs/D13.md asks for `a JSON file beside policy_budgets.json that your first round creates with a reason per job`. Established by measurement at both ends in a clone at the round's baseline: with the sibling list and the tree holding no list, the harness prints cfr_excluded=0.0; with the artifact registered at .claude/workflows/cfr_exclusions.json and the sibling removed, it prints the identical eight-merge numbers, which is the null control that shows the re-point moved the citation and not the metric. The perturbation the brief names still moves the number by exactly the excluded job's head count: `EXCLUSION_DROP=record` takes cfr_excluded 0.0 -> 1.0, record's eight of eight heads. And the fail-closed arm: with the artifact removed the harness raises, naming the registered path, rather than silently excluding nobody -- which is the always-green shape a metric `retaken minus the by-design reds` degrades into.
carries.remeasure: At your own merge base: run the D13 instrument (tools/audit/round5/D13/seat-a/dora_cfr.py) with its fixtures, then again with EXCLUSION_DROP naming the excluded job. If the second run's cfr_excluded does not move by that job's head count, the list is not being read. Then `python3 -c "import json;print(sorted(json.load(open('.claude/workflows/cfr_exclusions.json'))['excluded_jobs']))"` -- the list is a narrowing of the metric, so a round that GROWS it is making a deliberate edit, and an unjustified entry hides a real change failure rather than a by-design one.
carries.brief: Constraint on how the exclusion list is carried: it is ONE registered artifact at `.claude/workflows/cfr_exclusions.json`, a top-level object with an `excluded_jobs` map keyed by check-run name beside a `_comment`, in the shape .claude/workflows/policy_budgets.json takes. The instrument resolves it against the REPOSITORY, not against the seat, and raises when the map is missing or empty -- so a later round does not create a second list under a name of its choosing, and does not publish an un-excluded rate under the excluded rate's name. Each entry carries the reason and the citation it rests on; the one entry at the round-5 values is `record`, and the reason a later round must re-check rather than assume is that the red is by design only while the batch interval holds.

carries.from: the pull request fixing the round-6 D13-03 finding (#1407), which makes the round-4 DORA instrument (tools/audit/round4/D11/dora_keys.py, `cfr_keyings`) report the change-failure rate at BOTH keyings -- at the merge commit, where `.claude/workflows/cfr_exclusions.json` acts, and at the pull-request head, where a merge is gated -- and pins the pair in tests/entities.py
carries.control: The finding: the exclusion list's single entry `record` fails at 58 of the 67 merge commits in the window v6.6.0..e336cc2c and is SKIPPED at every one of the 67 pull-request heads, because its workflow gates the job to the non-pull_request event. So excluding it moves the merge-keyed rate 0.925 -> 0.09 and leaves the head-keyed rate at 0.134 -- the rate at the surface a merge is actually gated on, unchanged. Established by measurement at both ends: the instrument prints the un-excluded rate beside the excluded one from the same call over the same maps, so the exclusion's own delta is visible on each keying, and it is 56 merges at the merge keying and zero at the head keying; the round-6 finder harness measured the same figures, so the tracked instrument reproduces them rather than restating them. The perturbation that would have voided it: the names failing at the HEAD are `nightly-status` (7 of the 67) and `delivery-status` (2 of the 67), so one entry added for either moves the head keying and the pair stops separating the two surfaces. The key-set null control tests/entities.py already holds -- `excluded_jobs` is exactly the set holding `record`, with the gate jobs absent -- is what refuses that entry.
carries.remeasure: At your own merge base, run `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tools/audit/round4/D11/dora_keys.py` and read `cfr_merge_keyed` beside `cfr_head_keyed`; both are RESULT lines the instrument prints, and `cfr_exclusions` is printed with them so the list a rate came from is on the same screen. Or run tools/audit/round5/D13/seat-a/dora_cfr.py with `EXCLUSION_DROP=record`, which moves the merge-keyed rate by that job's head count. A rate reported at one keying only, or an entry added for a name that fails at the head, is this finding re-derived. The instrument pins its window (`D13_SINCE` / `D13_HEAD`), so a re-take names its own baseline instead of tracking a moving main.
carries.brief: Constraint on every change-failure rate a later round reports: the rate is TWO numbers -- the merge-keyed rate and the pull-request-head-keyed rate -- printed together and never one alone, because `.claude/workflows/cfr_exclusions.json` narrows only the merge keying while a merge is gated on the head keying. The artifact's `_keying` field states that rule for whoever edits the list, and tools/audit/briefs/D13.md's DORA item asks for the list without naming a keying, which is how the single-number report arose. A check-run name that fails at the pull-request head is a real gate red: it must NOT be added to the list, however much it costs the merge keying, and a report that names such a name as excluded is the escape this carry closes.
